ledger.note: 1180: Barbarossa breaks up the Duchy of Saxony and 'the Ascanians secured the see for Siegfried of Anhalt'; 'part of the diocesan territory' was upgraded to the Prince-Archbishopric. The page lists no towns and gives no area.
1186: the Gelnhausen Privilege 'recognized Bremen as a political body'; the city was 'de facto (since 1186) and de jure (since 1646) not part of the prince-archbishopric'.

region.text: Stedingen, north of Bremen in the Weser delta, where the archbishop was overlord

ledger.note: Christmas 1229: the first battle with the Stedingers. They had refused tithes and forced labour; Gerard II's brother Herman II of Lippe, installed at Schlutterburg, was killed; a Bremen council excommunicated the rebels on 17 March 1230 and put the land under interdict.

region.text: Stedingen, north of Bremen in the Weser delta, where the archbishop was overlord

ledger.note: 1234: the Stedingers are crushed. A second crusade under Henry I, Duke of Brabant, assembled at Bremen in spring 1234; the Stedinger forces under Detmar tom Diek and Tammo von Huntrop were defeated at Altenesch ('Thus the Stedingers met their end'). The first crusade of 1233 had failed to take the west bank on 6 July 1233. The page does not say who held the land afterwards.
1313: the residence moves to Vörde. 'Bremen did not tolerate the archbishop's residence within its walls'; the seats paragraph has Vörde as the seat of government from 1219.

region.text: the Land of Wursten, 15 km north of Bremerhaven

ledger.note: 9 August 1524: the Battle of Mulsum. 'The troops of Christopher the Spendthrift finally subjected the Wursten Frisians'; Wursten had been 'a rather autonomous Frisian farmers' republic' under only loose overlordship of the archbishopric.

region.text: the Land of Wursten, 15 km north of Bremerhaven

ledger.note: 1525: the Treaty of Stade, which ended the election of consuls.

region.text: the Land of Wursten, 15 km north of Bremerhaven

ledger.note: 1525: 'In 1525 the Wursten Consuls had to conclude the Treaty of Stade,' which incorporated Wursten into the prince-archbishopric (the Bremen page has the subjection in 1524). In 1567 Francis I of Saxe-Lauenburg gave up claims to Wursten and Bederkesa when his son Henry III was elected archbishop.

ledger.note: Summer 1627: Tilly invades and captures the southern parts; in 1628 he besieged Stade and on 5 May 1628 granted safe-conduct, so 'the whole archbishopric was in his hands'. The Danish king Christian IV had stationed troops in Stade in 1619-1620 and was beaten at Lutter on 27 August 1626. Swedish-backed forces reconquered parts in 1631.

notes: Four pages opened. The page gives no area or border: the circle between the Weser and the Elbe (45 km round Vörde, with Stade inside it) is the researcher's reading of 'about a third of the diocesan territory'; Land Hadeln (a Saxe-Lauenburg exclave in 1567) falls inside it and is not subtracted. Disagreements between pages: the Bremen infobox puts Dithmarschen in the territory 1145-1526, the Dithmarschen page says it was ceded after 1180 and rejected Bremen's overlordship, so it is not drawn; the seat moves to Vörde in 1219 (seats paragraph) or 1313 (narrative); Tilly's conquest is 1627 or 1628; the Swedish seizure is 1645 (infobox) or 1643-1645. Not settled: who held Stedingen after 1234, the location of Bederkesa, Verden's relation (a separate prince-bishopric, 1631 conquest), and the border of the diocesan territory. Needs dossiers: Duchy of Bremen (1648-1823), Land Wursten (small), Prince-Bishopric of Verden.
